description: F2P/P2P classification of this task's graded observations. F2P fail on the delivered state and pass after the reference repair; P2P pass on both. Measured in the task image, not derived from names. tests/grade.py reads this file and runs exactly the observations it names.

groups.requirement: with_section_cut_out skips the interval from start_time until end_time, including the frame at the start boundary, in video, mask and audio. Result duration is original duration minus removed length. It returns copied media and leaves the original unchanged.

General time_transform evaluates original media at time_func(t), leaves originals unchanged, defaults to no attachment transformation and clears duration/end. Explicit apply_to selects mask/audio by string or list, and keep_duration=True preserves timing; selected attachments receive the same policy. ImageClip overrides leave their image and own timing unchanged regardless of keep_duration, default to both attachments, and accept list selection; transformed general attachments default to cleared duration/end.

Zero-padding concatenation plays clips consecutively in supplied order, including correctly placed available soundtracks when other clips are silent. Chain returns source frames; compose centers inputs in the maximum-width/maximum-height canvas filled by bg_color. Duration is the sum of input durations and FPS is the highest input FPS. Media time within each input is relative to that input's sequence start.

with_start returns a copy, converts supported seconds/tuple/string times, and propagates to audio and mask. With default change_end=True end becomes start+duration; with False a known end is retained and duration becomes end-start. with_duration copies and propagates duration, updating end by default or start with change_end=False. Neither operation trims source media; originals retain metadata and samples.

subclipped returns copied media playing the original from start_time to end_time, with matching subclips of audio and mask. Supported time representations convert to seconds. Negative endpoints are relative to original duration; omitted end uses original duration. The resulting duration is end-start and its end is its start plus duration. Original media and metadata are unchanged.

with_speed_scaled multiplies playback speed by factor, or derives the factor from final_duration. It remaps video, audio and mask consistently, sets the scaled duration, and returns copied media without changing the original.

Original media and metadata are unchanged.
Clip.with_end returns a copy with end set (seconds, tuple or string), keeps start and sets duration to end - start; the audio and mask get the same timing; the original is unchanged.
Clip.with_duration returns a copy whose duration is set (any time format) and, with the default change_end=True, whose end becomes start + duration; the audio and mask get the same duration.
Clip.with_fps returns a copy with the new fps; with change_duration=True the speed changes so every frame is kept (halving the fps doubles the duration).
with_is_mask and with_memoize return copies with the is_mask / memoize attributes set; with_updated_frame_function returns a copy whose frames come from the new function.

Clip.iter_frames yields int(duration*fps) frames at times frame_index/fps, using the clip's fps by default; with_times=True yields (t, frame) pairs; dtype casts the frames; a clip without duration cannot be iterated.
Clip.is_playing(t) tells whether t lies between the clip's start and end (any time format); for a numpy array of times it returns False when none is in the clip, else a vector of per-time booleans.

clip[a:b] equals clip.subclipped(a, b); a third slice value is a speed coefficient (clip[:2:2] lasts half as long); a negative step plays the clip backwards; a tuple of slices concatenates the segments; a non-slice key returns the frame at that time.
Two clips are equal when they have the same number of frames and identical frames; clips are context managers whose exit calls close().
with_effects returns a copy of the clip with the effects applied in list order, each effect being copied before it is applied, and leaves the original clip unchanged.
with_volume_scaled(factor) multiplies the audio volume by factor (see afx.MultiplyVolume), optionally only between start_time and end_time.

transform(func) returns a clip whose frame at t is func(get_frame, t); time_transform(time_func) returns a clip whose frame at t is the original frame at time_func(t); by default neither changes the mask or the audio.
subclipped refuses a start_time at or after the clip's duration and an end_time beyond it with ValueError; a negative start_time counts from the end; times may be strings or tuples.
convert_to_seconds converts seconds, (min, sec), (hour, min, sec) tuples and 'HH:MM:SS.ss' strings (a comma also works as decimal separator) into seconds, as in its documented examples.

find_extension maps documented codecs to file extensions and returns an extension unchanged; deprecated_version_of returns a function that warns and delegates; ffmpeg_escape_filename prefixes names starting with '-'; no_display_available reports whether a display is available.
cross_platform_popen_params returns the given Popen parameters (with Windows-only additions on Windows); subprocess_call runs a command and raises IOError when it fails.
close_all_clips closes every clip found in the given objects (a dict of names to objects) whose kind is in types.

requires_duration raises ValueError for a clip without duration; requires_fps raises ValueError without fps; convert_parameter_to_seconds converts the named arguments with convert_to_seconds; outplace applies the method to a copy; use_clip_fps_by_default fills fps from the clip; add_mask_if_none adds a mask; apply_to_mask / apply_to_audio also apply the method to the mask / audio.
An Effect subclass implements apply(clip) returning the new clip; with_effects copies the effect before applying it; Effect.copy returns an independent shallow copy; Effect is abstract.

AccelDecel(new_duration, abruptness, soonness) remaps time so the result lasts new_duration (default the clip's duration), starts at the first frame and ends at the last; abruptness 0 has no effect; a negative soonness raises ValueError.
BlackAndWhite desaturates the frames: every channel becomes the RGB-weighted mean (weights [1,1,1] by default, 'CRT_phosphor' preset), normalised to sum 1 with preserve_luminosity.
Blink(duration_on, duration_off) makes the clip's mask visible for duration_on seconds then invisible for duration_off seconds, repeatedly (a mask is added when missing).

Crop keeps the rectangular region x1,y1 (top-left) to x2,y2 (bottom-right), in pixels; width/height and x_center/y_center can replace corners; omitted bounds default to the clip's edges; the mask is cropped too.

CrossFadeIn/CrossFadeOut(duration) make the clip appear/disappear progressively over duration seconds by fading its mask from/to 0 (a mask is added when missing); a clip without duration raises ValueError.
EvenSize crops the clip so its width and height are even (an even clip is unchanged).

FadeIn(duration, initial_color) fades the clip from initial_color (black by default, 0 for masks) over the first duration seconds; FadeOut(duration, final_color) fades to final_color over the last duration seconds; FadeOut needs a duration.

Freeze(t, freeze_duration | total_duration) inserts a still of the frame at t lasting freeze_duration (or total_duration - clip.duration); t='end' freezes the last frame; without either duration it raises ValueError.
FreezeRegion(t, region | outside_region | mask) freezes one region of the frame at time t while the rest stays animated.
GammaCorrection(gamma) maps each value v to 255*(v/255)**gamma; LumContrast(lum, contrast, contrast_threshold) maps v to v + lum + contrast*(v - threshold), clipped to [0, 255].
HeadBlur(fx, fy, radius, intensity) blurs a disc of the given radius around (fx(t), fy(t)) and leaves the rest of the frame unchanged.
InvertColors replaces each value v by 255 - v (1 - v for masks); MultiplyColor(factor) multiplies the colours by factor, capped at 255.
Loop(n | duration) plays the clip repeatedly: n times (duration n*clip.duration) or for duration seconds; a clip without duration raises ValueError.
MakeLoopable(overlap_duration) makes the clip fade in at its own end; the result lasts clip.duration - overlap_duration.
Margin draws a margin of margin_size pixels (or left/right/top/bottom) around the frame in the given colour; opacity below 1 makes the margin partly transparent through a mask.
MaskColor(color, threshold, stiffness) adds a mask that is transparent (0) where the frame has the given colour and opaque (1) elsewhere; with a threshold the mask is d**s/(threshold**s + d**s).
MasksAnd/MasksOr combine a clip with another clip or array by the minimum/maximum of pixel values, as in their documented red/green examples.
MirrorX flips the frames horizontally and MirrorY vertically, the mask too by default.
MultiplySpeed(factor | final_duration) plays the clip factor times faster (or so it lasts final_duration) and divides its duration accordingly.
Painting(saturation, black) transforms each frame into a painting-like image of the same size.

Resize(new_size | height | width) resizes the clip to (width, height) pixels, by a scale factor, or to a given height or width keeping the aspect ratio; new_size may be a function of time; the mask is resized too; a uniform colour stays the same.

Rotate(angle, unit) rotates the frames anticlockwise by angle degrees (or radians); multiples of 90 with expand keep every pixel; expand=False keeps the input size; an unknown resample raises ValueError.
Scroll(w, h, x_speed, y_speed, x_start, y_start) shows a w x h window moving over the frame at the given speeds from the given start.
SlideIn/SlideOut(duration, side) set a time-dependent position so the clip enters from / leaves through the given side of a CompositeVideoClip over duration seconds.
SuperSample(d, n_frames) replaces the frame at t by the mean of n_frames equally spaced frames in [t-d, t+d].
TimeMirror plays the clip backwards; TimeSymmetrize plays it forwards then backwards (twice the duration); both need a duration.
moviepy.video.fx exposes every documented video effect class and moviepy.audio.fx every audio effect class, both available as vfx and afx from moviepy.
AudioDelay(offset, n_repeats, decay) repeats the sound n_repeats times every offset seconds with volumes linearly spaced from 1 to decay.

AudioFadeIn(duration) starts mute and reaches the normal level after duration seconds; AudioFadeOut fades to zero over the last duration seconds; durations accept time strings; both apply to a video's audio too.
AudioLoop(n_loops | duration) plays the sound n_loops times or for duration seconds.
AudioNormalize scales the sound so its maximum volume becomes 1 (0 dB); a silent clip is unchanged.
MultiplyVolume(factor, start_time, end_time) multiplies the volume by factor, by default over the whole clip; MultiplyStereoVolume(left, right) multiplies the left and right channels separately.
A VideoClip built from frame_function(t) -> HxWx3 array has size (width, height), w, h, aspect_ratio w/h, n_frames duration*fps; a mask clip (is_mask=True) has greyscale frames.
Copying a VideoClip (with_* methods work on copies) leaves the original's attributes, mask and audio unchanged.
save_frame(filename, t) writes the frame at time t (any time format) to an image file; with_mask stores the mask as alpha in PNGs.

write_videofile writes the clip to a video file with the given (or the clip's) fps, choosing the codec from the extension; the clip's audio is written as the soundtrack; reading the file back gives the same size, fps and duration.
write_images_sequence writes one image per frame at the given fps using the name_format pattern and returns the list of file names.
write_gif writes the clip as an animated GIF with the given (or the clip's) fps.
with_effects_on_subclip(effects, start_time, end_time) applies the effects to the part of the clip between start_time and end_time and keeps the rest.
image_transform(image_func) replaces each frame by image_func(frame); apply_to=['mask'] also transforms the mask.
fill_array pads a smaller array with ones at the bottom/right, or crops a larger one from the bottom/right, to the requested shape.
with_background_color(size, color, pos, opacity) places the clip on a coloured background of the given size (default the clip's size), centred by default.

with_audio returns a copy with the audio attached and without_audio a copy without it; with_mask() adds a solid mask of 1.0 (or the given mask) and without_mask removes it; with_opacity multiplies the mask by the opacity.
with_position sets the clip's position in compositions: pixel coordinates, keywords such as 'center' and 'top', fractions with relative=True, or a function of t; with_layer_index sets the layer.
resized, rotated and cropped are shortcuts for vfx.Resize, vfx.Rotate and vfx.Crop.

to_ImageClip(t) returns an ImageClip of the frame at t (any time format, with the mask by default); to_mask(canal) returns a mask clip from one colour channel scaled to 0-1; to_RGB turns a mask into an RGB clip.
clip1 + clip2 concatenates, clip1 | clip2 places them side by side, clip1 / clip2 stacks them, clip @ angle rotates and clip & mask uses mask as the clip's mask; clip * n loops.
DataVideoClip(data, data_to_frame, fps) shows data_to_frame(data[i]) as frame i; its duration is len(data)/fps.
UpdatedVideoClip(world) calls world.update() until world.clip_t reaches t and shows world.to_frame().

ImageClip shows a picture (an RGB array or an image file) at all times; an RGBA image with transparent=True gives the clip a mask from the alpha channel; is_mask makes a mask clip; image_transform on an ImageClip returns an ImageClip.
ColorClip(size, color) shows one colour (black by default); with is_mask=True the colour is a float between 0 and 1.

TextClip renders text with the given (or Pillow's default) font: method='label' sizes the clip to the text, method='caption' wraps the text in the given size; color, bg_color, margin and duration are applied; transparent text clips get a mask.
BitmapClip(bitmap_frames, fps) builds frames from rows of colour letters (R, G, B, ...) and to_bitmap returns the same representation.

CompositeVideoClip layers clips in increasing layer_index order (later clips on top for equal layers) on a bg_color background of the given size (default the first clip's size); masks make parts transparent; its duration is the maximum end of the clips; its fps is the highest fps; the clips' audio is mixed.
With use_bgclip=True the first clip is the background on which the others are drawn; it is excluded from the automatic duration.
clips_array arranges a matrix of clips in rows and columns; smaller clips are centred in their cell on bg_color; row heights and column widths default to the largest clip in each row and column.

concatenate_videoclips plays the clips one after another; padding adds a gap (or with method='compose' a negative overlap) between consecutive clips; a transition clip is played between each two clips.

An AudioClip built from frame_function(t) has nchannels 1 for mono and 2 for stereo and returns one sample (or one row per channel pair) per time; iter_chunks, to_soundarray and max_volume read the sound at the given fps.
write_audiofile writes the sound to a file (codec from the extension, fps default the clip's fps); reading it back gives the same duration and channel count.
AudioArrayClip(array, fps) plays an Nx1 or Nx2 array at fps samples per second; its duration is N/fps.
CompositeAudioClip mixes clips that start at their own start times (starts/ends); its duration is the latest end; concatenate_audioclips plays clips one after another; audio + audio concatenates.
from moviepy import * exposes the clip classes, compositing functions, effect packages vfx/afx, Effect, convert_to_seconds, video tools and file clips.

compute_position(clip1_size, clip2_size, pos, relative) returns the top-left corner of clip 1 on clip 2 for pixel positions, keywords ('center', 'left', 'right', 'top', 'bottom') and relative fractions; None means (0, 0).

convert_masks_to_RGB converts a mask clip to RGB before the call; audio_video_effect applies an audio effect to a video clip's audio and returns the video clip; preprocess_args applies a function to the named arguments; convert_path_to_string turns path-like arguments into strings.
compose_on(background, t) returns the clip's frame at t drawn on the background picture at the clip's position, accounting for the clip's mask.
ImageClip.transform returns an animated VideoClip (no longer an ImageClip) whose frame at t is func(get_frame, t).
TextClip can read its text from a file (filename), and with transparent=False it has no mask.
CompositeVideoClip.playing_clips(t) lists the clips playing at t; with is_mask=True the composite is a mask clip; with bg_color=None the unfilled regions are transparent through the composite mask.
A sequence of images written by write_images_sequence can be loaded back as a clip of the given fps (ImageSequenceClip, documented in the loading guide).
